title: Fit a restricted bridge coefficient path — rbridge
code: # Reproducible synthetic demonstration: 100 observations, eight predictors. set.seed(2019) beta <- c(3, 1.5, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0) p <- length(beta) beta <- matrix(beta, nrow = p, ncol = 1) n <- 100 X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p) y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta + rnorm(n)) # A user-specified sum of standardized slopes: b[1] + b[2] + b[5] = 6.5. # This target is illustrative; it is not asserted to equal the generating sum. R1.mat <- matrix(c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 1) r1.vec <- matrix(6.5, nrow = 1, ncol = 1) # A second standardized-slope contrast: -b[1] + b[2] + b[5] = 0.5. R2.mat <- matrix(c(-1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 1) r2.vec <- matrix(0.5, nrow = 1, ncol = 1) # Impose both independent restrictions together. R3.mat <- rbind(R1.mat, R2.mat) r3.vec <- matrix(c(6.5, 0.5), ncol = 1) # Alternatively, set the five inactive generating slopes to zero. p.active <- which(beta != 0) R4.mat <- diag(p)[-p.active, , drop = FALSE] r4.vec <- matrix(rep(0, p - length(p.active)), ncol = 1)  # Five penalties keep this help example fast; the default is 100. model1 <- rbridge(X, y, q = 1, R = R1.mat, r = r1.vec, nlambda = 5) model2 <- rbridge(X, y, q = 1, R = R2.mat, r = r2.vec, nlambda = 5) model3 <- rbridge(X, y, q = 1, R = R3.mat, r = r3.vec, nlambda = 5) model4 <- rbridge(X, y, q = 1, R = R4.mat, r = r4.vec, nlambda = 5) # Rows include the intercept; columns correspond to fitted penalties. dim(model1$betas) #> [1] 9 5 # Extract the second fitted penalty exactly; no interpolation is performed. selected <- model1$lambda[2] coefficients <- coef(model1, s = selected) coefficients #>             26.8035044402758 #> (Intercept)     1.288482e-02 #> V1              2.983157e+00 #> V2              1.579113e+00 #> V3              5.156258e-05 #> V4             -2.378501e-05 #> V5              1.993807e+00 #> V6             -3.666309e-04 #> V7              3.309060e-05 #> V8              0.000000e+00 predict(model1, newx = X[1:5, , drop = FALSE], s = selected) #> [1]  -1.6230925   0.3471289  -1.5657036   2.6335804 -10.4459031 # Convert returned slopes to standardized slopes before checking the target. x_centered <- sweep(X, 2, colMeans(X), "-") x_rms <- sqrt(colMeans(x_centered^2)) standardized_slopes <- coefficients[-1, 1] * x_rms as.numeric(R1.mat %*% standardized_slopes - r1.vec) #> [1] 0
